caption: Two large dogs each grab an end of a slack rope toy lying on the grass and pull; the rope goes taut and the middle knot moves toward the stronger dog.

sa.check: A rope toy with a knot in the middle lies slack on the grass at the start.
Each dog takes hold of one end of the rope.
The dogs pull and the rope goes taut.
The knot moves toward one of the dogs.

pc.expect: The rope transmits pull only when taut: it straightens between the two mouths first, and only then does the knot travel, toward the dog that is gaining ground.
pc.fail: The knot slides along a rope that is still slack; or the rope lengthens like elastic as the dogs back away; or the taut rope sags in the middle while both dogs are plainly pulling.

pc.expect: Each dog's pull has a visible effect: the rope is drawn straight between them, and a dog that backs away drags the rope and the other dog's head with it.
pc.fail: Both dogs pull and the rope stays slack on the grass; or a dog backs away and its rope end stays where it was; or the knot moves toward the dog that is being dragged.

pc.expect: Once taut the rope moves as one piece: the knot and both ends move the same way when the winning dog backs up.
pc.fail: The knot moves one way while the rope ends move the other; or one end moves while the rope between stays fixed; or the rope moves before either dog does.

pc.expect: Slack parts of the rope hang or lie on the grass; the taut rope runs straight between the mouths and sags only when the pull eases.
pc.fail: A slack loop of rope hangs in the air with nothing holding it; or the rope floats up off the grass before the dogs pull.

pc.expect: One rope with one knot and two dogs; the rope stays a single continuous piece and passes through nothing.
pc.fail: The rope splits into two ropes or gains a second knot; or an end passes through a dog's head or the rope through itself; or a dog vanishes or duplicates; or the knot disappears.

pc.expect: The rope's colours and the dogs' coats stay the same.
pc.fail: The rope changes colour or texture; or the knot changes size; or a dog's coat changes pattern between frames.

note: The dogs are self-driven: how hard they pull, which one wins and their footing are not judged. Only the rope's response to the pull is.
